HLP_101: Pac-Man was born on May 22, 1980 at Namco, in Japan.
HLP_102: Through its many editions, adaptations and tributes, its objectives have always remained the same:
HLP_103: eat pacgums, survive, escape the ghosts or hunt them once empowered by the
HLP_104: super-pacgum, collect bonuses, start over on the next level.
HLP_105: - If the ghosts catch Pac-Man, he loses a life and reappears at the center of the level.
HLP_106: - If Pac-Man eats a super-pacgum, he becomes a ghost predator for a few moments.
HLP_107: - If a ghost is caught, its spirit returns to its starting point where it regains a tangible form.
HLP_108: - If time runs out, $TIMEOUTCONSEQUENCES$. This effect is configurable.
HLP_109: - After eating all the pacgums within the time limit, Pac-Man advances to the next level.
HLP_110: - Eating pacgums, ghosts or bonuses earns points.
HLP_111: - Every $NEWLIFEPOINTS$ points, Pac-Man gains an extra life.
HLP_112: - There is no cheat mode. Or maybe there is. This information is not available here.

INT_021:
Gospel of the Pac-Amama,
Book of Platitudes
INT_026:
Apocryphal verses, lost, forgotten,
rediscovered, recycled as kindling,
and faithfully transcribed from memory
by the Scribe Oprius the Madcap
INT_051:
Yet another flativerse.

I've stopped counting them. I don't know if I'll ever get out.
My journey began $YEARS$ $YPLURAL$, $MONTHS$ $MPLURAL$ and $DAYS$ $DPLURAL$ ago.
It was stupid. Some old guy, a quest, a promise of adventure.

I should have listened to my mother.
Don't ask me what she said. I wasn't listening.
Who am I even talking to?

I'm going mad. All these flativerses, one after another, by the thousands,
by the millions, by the billions perhaps.
If anyone reads this, help me.
I want to get out of here.
INT_070: I saw a new object appear:
INT_071: I saw some new objects appear:
INT_082: the brown crate contained an hourglass
INT_083: the dark green crate contained a plant, perhaps sage
INT_084: the purple crate contained a bomb
INT_085: the red crate contained a hair bow, and I have no hair
INT_086: the white crate contained a hat
INT_087: the light green crate contained some sticky goo
INT_088: the yellow crate was empty, but I felt I had been given an extra chance
INT_092: Using the hourglass made me feel less pressed for time.
INT_093: The sage drove the ghosts away; they must hate the stuff.
INT_094: The bomb blast travels far down the corridors; it is dangerous for them and for me.
INT_095: I put the bow on my head, felt very different, and saw the world through rose-tinted glasses.
INT_096: I put the hat on my head, felt as though I had entered another reality, and the pacgums tasted metallic.
INT_097: The sticky goo covered me and carried me into another reality, where the pacgums tasted salty and creatures with strange appendages chased me.
INT_10102:
This flativerse was different.

Wider corridors, a strange layout, and I felt an odd
urgency to explore it, as though my time was running
out.

I don't know what to make of it, but after decades
of wandering through identical flativerses, this
change gives me hope. Could these differences mean
my exile is finally coming to an end?

My friend Phil used to say:
"Anything different is good."
